triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated. Opening edge rests on a ruled tier-1 speech frame standing in the cited verse's own bytes: וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר byte-collates at oshb:Job.26.1 (verse-initial vaya'an family, sweep 27 book-wide; the pointed 3-word string byte-sweeps 9 verses: 3:2, 6:1, 9:1, 12:1, 16:1, 19:1, 21:1, 23:1, 26:1), corroborated — not driven — by the PE the inventory records after Job.25.6 (pmarks_Job.json marks Job.25.6 = PE; petuchah named, never conflated with SAMEKH, single-witness stated, mark-follows-verse wording correct, tier-3). Closing edge at Job.26.4|Job.26.5 rests on the 2ms-to-3rd-person address shift (§6 tier-1): all five 2ms qatal forms byte-collate at their verses (עָזַ֥רְתָּ, ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ at oshb:Job.26.2; יָּ֭עַצְתָּ, הוֹדָֽעְתָּ at oshb:Job.26.3; הִגַּ֣דְתָּ at oshb:Job.26.4), and WEB Job.26.5 is third-person throughout. The medium_low band is honest rather than masking: the shift is gradual at the very edge — the row itself shows יָצְאָ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ closing Job.26.4 with a 3fs verb plus a trailing 2ms suffix — and the row sits inside the strategy §8 crux-5 disarray region. No K/Q lies inside Job.26.1-4 (pmarks kq lists ch26 only at 26:12 and 26:14), so nothing is undisclosed; both curly-quoted WEB runs are verbatim in their exact cited verses (Job.26.2, Job.26.4) with no +-1 slack needed. Neither over-stated nor materially under-stated.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale carries a writer-part reference ('the rest of the part') instead of a verse-anchored scope statement.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale reads '-- the MT frame this row and the rest of the part follow through the third-cycle disarray of chapters 25-28'. 'the part' is workflow/administrative register (the writer part is strategy §9 p10 Job.25.1-Job.28.28); the register law requires row prose to describe the text and to anchor scope by verse. E-18 arm re-derived from bytes and TRUE, so this is cosmetic only: over chapters 25-31 the verse-initial formula members are vaya'an at oshb:Job.25.1 and oshb:Job.26.1 (וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר), vayosef at oshb:Job.27.1 and oshb:Job.29.1 (וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר, the two byte-identical), and the only frame vayomer is the interior quotation frame at oshb:Job.28.28 — i.e. the MT frame does govern through Job.28.28.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only: replace 'this row and the rest of the part' with a verse-anchored scope ('this row and the material through Job.28.28'). No span, seam or confidence change.

triggers.grounds: The medium_low label itself is honest and not masking a byte-defective warrant. Opening edge at Job.26.4|Job.26.5 is the ruled tier-1 address shift, and every byte claim in the row re-derives: the splices at oshb:Job.26.5, oshb:Job.26.6, oshb:Job.26.12 (carrying the ketiv and qere adjacent, as the staged extract does), oshb:Job.26.13 and both halves of the elided oshb:Job.26.14 run all collate at BYTE tier; the K/Q digits match the inventory exactly (pmarks_Job.json kq: Job.26.12 = 1 note, Job.26.14 = 2 notes) and the 'his way/his ways; his power/his mighty acts' description matches those notes; the SAMEKH claim is real and correctly formed (pmarks marks Job.26.14 = SAMEKH; setumah named, single-witness, mark-follows-verse); the curly-quoted WEB run is verbatim in its exact cited verse Job.26.14; 'five times the length' is arithmetically true (Job.26.5-14 = 10 verses against Job.25.2-3 = 2). The low band is warranted by the strategy §8 crux-5 question the row's own rejected alternative names (whether the cosmological catalog is Job's or Bildad's). A separate finding records the closing-edge warrant gap; that gap corroborates the low band rather than showing the label over-stated.

findings.claim: The row's closing edge at Job.26.14|Job.27.1 names no tier-1 warrant; the only structural signal offered there is the tier-3 SAMEKH, which the book law bars from driving a seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale closes: 'The catalog closes on a gnomic reflection: ... and a SAMEKH mark follows it in the same inventory (oshb:Job.26.14 (setumah, single-witness))'. 'the catalog closes on a gnomic reflection' is a content-shape observation, not a ruled signal, so the mark stands alone at that edge, and strategy §4 plus the campaign addendum make parashah marks in the Writings tier-3 weak corroboration at most, never a driver. The ruled tier-1 signal sits one verse later and is cited nowhere in the row (neither prose nor boundary_evidence_refs, which stop at oshb:Job.26.1): oshb:Job.27.1 = וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר, verse-initial vayosef (sweep 3 book-wide: 27:1, 29:1, 36:1) and byte-identical to oshb:Job.29.1 — the signal the next row M8-Job-106 does argue. Cross-row coherence therefore holds (the neighbours are compatible, not contradictory) and the seam itself stands; the defect is in this row's stated grounds.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: add the tier-1 closing warrant to boundary_rationale and to boundary_evidence_refs (oshb:Job.27.1, the verse-initial vayosef opening Job's mashal resumption), keeping the SAMEKH as disclosed tier-3 corroboration. No span or seam change.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated. The opening warrant is byte-verified and is the strongest object bearing on strategy §8 crux 6: the two-word deictic opening זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק byte-collates at oshb:Job.27.13 and at oshb:Job.20.29, and its book-wide sweep is 2 verses at BYTE tier (also 2 at accent-stripped and 2 word-bound at skeleton) — 'the object's only two members' is true with its digit adjacent, and the form is verse-initial in both members. The paseq digit is true (pmarks_Job.json paseq Job.27.13 = 2 segs; cited count-only, single-witness, no position claim). The 'no new speech formula at this seam' disclosure re-derives: over chs 25-31 the only verse-initial vaya'an are 25:1 and 26:1, the only vayosef 27:1 and 29:1, and the only frame vayomer 28:28 — nothing at 27:13. Every Hebrew run collates at BYTE tier at its cited verse, including the full oshb:Job.20.29 quotation; both curly-quoted WEB runs (Job.27.13, Job.20.29) and the closing run at Job.27.23 are verbatim in their exact cited verses; the row's span 27:13-27:23 crosses the K/Q at Job.27.15 but no quoted span touches it, so no disclosure was owed. medium_low is the honest band for a seam inside the crux-6 Zophar-toned material.

findings.class: tier-conflation (pointed form displayed for a skeleton-tier shared object)
findings.claim: 'both verses open with' the displayed pointed second-colon form is byte-false for Job.20.29; only the consonantal skeleton is shared.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale: 'the parallel continues into the second colon, where both verses open with וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת (skeleton sweep: 3 book-wide, adding Job.31.2)'. Re-swept with the count object named: that pointed run byte-sweeps 2 verses (oshb:Job.27.13 and oshb:Job.31.2 = וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת, identical bytes) and accent-stripped 2; oshb:Job.20.29's second colon opens with the distinct pointed form וְנַחֲלַ֖ת, which the row itself displays correctly a few words earlier inside its full quotation of that verse. The digit and tier in the same parenthesis are TRUE (word-bound skeleton sweep 3: Job.20.29, Job.27.13, Job.31.2), and the seam rests on the byte-verified two-word formula, not on this echo — hence low, not medium. Neighbour row M8-Job-107 (review_revision 2) states the same object correctly ('at byte/accent-stripped tier the count narrows to 2 ... while Job.20.29 carries the distinct accent-stripped form'), so the corpus is internally inconsistent on one object across an adjacent pair.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only: say the second colon of both verses opens with the same CONSONANTAL form (skeleton sweep: 3 — Job.20.29, Job.27.13, Job.31.2) and name Job.20.29's distinct pointing, as M8-Job-107 already does. No span or confidence change.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated, and the tier-4 lane is clean. The opening warrant stands in Job.28.1's own bytes — the asseverative particle כִּ֤י יֵ֣שׁ byte-collates at oshb:Job.28.1 (WEB Job.28.1 'Surely there is a mine for silver'), and the row argues the miners' scene shift (§6 tier-1 'explicit participant/scene shifts'), the very framing strategy §8 crux 7 uses ('ki 28:1 opens a mining excursus'). The coinciding WEB/MT chapter division is referred to descriptively ('No new speech formula opens chapter 28') and never cited as evidence, so no tier-4 driver. That disclosure re-derives from bytes: ch28 carries no verse-initial vaya'an or vayosef, and its only frame vayomer (28:28) is interior. Mark and seg digits are true (pmarks_Job.json marks Job.28.11 = PE, petuchah correctly named and not conflated; paseq Job.28.3 = 1 and Job.28.4 = 1, i.e. the two segs claimed, count-only with no position claim); all three curly-quoted WEB runs are verbatim in their exact cited verses (Job.28.4, Job.28.9, Job.28.11) and the closing Hebrew run collates at BYTE tier at oshb:Job.28.11; ch28 carries no K/Q at all. medium_low is the honest band for a seam inside crux 7. A separate finding records the closing-edge warrant gap, which does not make the low band over-stated.

findings.claim: The row's closing edge at Job.28.11|Job.28.12 names only the tier-3 PE; the ruled tier-1 refrain standing one verse later is cited neither in prose nor in refs.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale offers, at the back edge, only 'A PE mark follows in the single-witness inventory (oshb:Job.28.11 (petuchah, single-witness)), and two paseq segs mark verses 3 and 4 within the row'. Both mark claims are TRUE against pmarks_Job.json, but strategy §4 and the campaign addendum make Writings parashah marks tier-3 weak corroboration at most and never a driver, and paseq is a count-only seg layer. The ruled tier-1 signal is the wisdom-poem refrain position at Job.28.12 (§6 'refrain positions (28:12/28:20)'; §2d refrain sweep 2, both in ch28): oshb:Job.28.12 opens וְֽ֭הַחָכְמָה מֵאַ֣יִן תִּמָּצֵ֑א. It appears nowhere in this row's boundary_rationale or boundary_evidence_refs, while the next row M8-Job-110 argues exactly that refrain — so the neighbours are compatible and the seam stands, but this row's own stated warrant for its back edge is tier-3 only.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair only: name the Job.28.12 refrain position as the closing tier-1 warrant in boundary_rationale and add web:Job.28.12 / oshb:Job.28.12 to boundary_evidence_refs, keeping the PE as disclosed tier-3 corroboration. No span or seam change.

triggers.grounds: TEST 1 (register law) fails: boundary_rationale refers to a neighbouring chunk by position rather than by verse — 'the same ba-plus-infinitive-construct subordinate form as two that precede it inside the preceding row' — and adds further process register in the same field ('the chunked edge at Job.29.6|Job.29.7', 'this row's own opening edge', 'the row before it'). TEST 2 (E-18 arm) re-derived from bytes and TRUE, so the defect is cosmetic, not evidential: בְּצֵ֣אתִי byte-collates at oshb:Job.29.7, בְּהִלּ֣וֹ at oshb:Job.29.3 and בִּרְחֹ֣ץ at oshb:Job.29.6 — all three bet + infinitive construct — and Job.29.3 and Job.29.6 do fall inside the previous row's span (M8-Job-113 = Job.29.1-Job.29.6); the exclusion of Job.29.5 is correct, בְּע֣וֹד being bet on the free-standing adverb, not an infinitive construct; and the finite qatal resumption רָא֣וּנִי נְעָרִ֣ים וְנֶחְבָּ֑אוּ byte-collates at oshb:Job.29.8, one verse past the row's edge, as claimed. True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.class: E-06 register bleed / E-18 positional cross-row reference
findings.claim: A cross-row reference is made positionally ('inside the preceding row') and the seam is described in chunking-process register ('the chunked edge'), where the register law requires verse-anchored text description.
findings.grounds: The offending strings are 'two that precede it inside the preceding row, Job.29.3 ... and Job.29.6 ...' and 'the chunked edge at Job.29.6|Job.29.7'. The underlying grammar and location claims are byte-true (see the trigger grounds: the three bet + infinitive-construct forms and the Job.29.5 exclusion all collate at BYTE tier at their verses, and both cited forms lie inside Job.29.1-Job.29.6), and the row's other work is sound — the opening scene shift is a §6 tier-1 signal, the WEB runs at Job.29.7 and Job.29.8 are verbatim in their exact cited verses, and the syntactic rival at Job.29.7|Job.29.8 is disclosed on both sides of the seam (M8-Job-113 discloses it identically), so cross-row coherence holds. Cosmetic register only.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only: 'two that precede it at Job.29.3 ... and Job.29.6 ...' and 'the edge at Job.29.6|Job.29.7'. No span, seam or confidence change.

triggers.grounds: TEST 1 (register law) fails: boundary_rationale cites campaign tooling documentation as such — 'this is the skeleton-is-substring-not-root hazard the toolkit documents' — which is process register, not text description (and unlike a bare inventory disclosure it names no verse or witness). TEST 2 re-derived from bytes and TRUE, so the defect is cosmetic: the self-quotation frame וָ֭אֹמַר byte-collates at oshb:Job.29.18 and byte-sweeps 1 verse, while at accent-stripped tier it sweeps exactly 2 verses — oshb:Job.29.18 and oshb:Job.38.11 (וָאֹמַ֗ר) — both verse-initial, so both 'accent-stripped sweep: 2' and 'the two differ in their accents, so not byte-identical to each other' are exact. The wider skeleton SUBSTRING search does over-collect to 4 verses by adding oshb:Job.22.13 וְֽ֭אָמַרְתָּ (waw + 2ms perfect, verse-initial, in Eliphaz's third speech) and oshb:Job.7.4 וְאָמַ֗רְתִּי (waw + 1cs perfect, word 3 of its verse under the maqaf-free tokenization) — a word-bound skeleton sweep returns 2. True claim in workflow register -> low.

findings.claim: The boundary_rationale names campaign tooling documentation ('the toolkit documents') inside the seam argument.
findings.grounds: The string is '-- this is the skeleton-is-substring-not-root hazard the toolkit documents'. The methodological point and every digit around it re-derive true from bytes (see the trigger grounds: accent-stripped sweep 2 verse-initial members, skeleton substring 4, word-bound skeleton 2), and the exclusivity phrase 'the only one of the two spoken in Job's own voice' carries its digit adjacently and is true, Job.38.11 sitting inside the YHWH speech opened at oshb:Job.38.1. Cosmetic register only; no evidence defect.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to boundary_rationale only: state the hazard as a property of the search ('a skeleton search is a consonantal substring search, so it also catches ...') with no reference to campaign documentation. No span, seam or confidence change.

findings.claim: literature_type_guess labels the unit with the 'phoenix' rendering of Job.29.18, which neither staged witness carries and which the row's own rationale contradicts.
findings.grounds: literature_type_guess reads 'Job's hope of enduring blessing like renewed phoenix'. The substrate word is וְ֝כַח֗וֹל at oshb:Job.29.18 (byte-spliced), and the translation witness reads 'I will count my days as the sand' (WEB Job.29.18, verbatim in the row's own curly-quoted run); a WEB phrase sweep for 'phoenix' returns 0 verses book-wide, while 'as the sand' returns 1 (Job.29.18). The row's own boundary_rationale summarizes the images as 'nest, sand, spread roots, renewed bow', so the label contradicts the row's reading. Strategy §5 confines cross-tradition material to prose metadata, never evidence, and no disclosure accompanies the rendering here. Non-driver field: the seam and confidence do not rest on it — hence low.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair to literature_type_guess only: relabel from the substrate reading (e.g. 'Job's hope of dying at home with days numberless as sand'), or keep the alternative rendering only with an explicit cross-tradition disclosure. No span, seam or confidence change.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated low band with sound grounds. The stated reason for the low band is honest and matches the bytes: the opening edge at Job.30.31|Job.31.1 carries no ruled §6 tier-1 signal, only the genre turn to legal self-asseveration standing in Job.31.1's own bytes (בְּ֭רִית כָּרַ֣תִּי לְעֵינָ֑י, byte-collated at oshb:Job.31.1), and the row says so ('No new speech formula opens Job.31 -- it remains inside the Job.29.1 vayosef span'), which re-derives true (the nearest verse-initial formulas are vayosef at oshb:Job.29.1 and the colophon at Job.31.40; nothing in ch30-31 between them). The coinciding chapter division is referred to descriptively and never cited as evidence, so the tier-4 lane is clean. The closing edge at Job.31.4|Job.31.5 is by contrast a ruled tier-1 protasis block, and the digit-bearing claim behind it re-derives EXACTLY: the bare conditional particle אִם (byte-collated at oshb:Job.31.5) sweeps 17 word-bound tokens over 17 verses inside ch31 — 31:5, 7, 9, 13, 16, 19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 26, 29, 31, 33, 36, 38, 39, every token the verse-initial hireq particle, first member Job.31.5 and last Job.31.39, matching strategy §2d — with NO member in Job.31.1-4, so 'use no conditional particle at all' is byte-true. The two disclosures inside the rejected alternative are also true: אִם לֹ֣א at oshb:Job.31.36 is a member of the particle-token count and is an oath affirmation, not a protasis (§2e-b), and Job.31.35 opens instead on מִ֤י יִתֶּן (byte-collated and verse-initial at oshb:Job.31.35, byte-unique to that verse at this pointing) with no conditional particle. Both curly-quoted WEB runs (Job.31.1, Job.31.4) are verbatim in their exact cited verses; no K/Q lies inside Job.31.1-4 (pmarks kq for ch31 is 31:11 and 31:20); no mark is claimed and none exists at these verses, absence correctly left unused. No frontier flag is warranted — the weakness is a seam-strength question, not a canon/authorship one. If anything the band is conservative rather than over-stated, since the closing edge is tier-1; low is defensible on the unwarranted opening edge alone.
